title: Bridge and Letter
premise: In the river city of Vellamark, newly annexed by a victorious empire, Felix Oyelaran is summoned to repair the observatory's master clock, whose stopped hands have become a symbol of the old regime's fall. While working, he uncovers letters hidden in the clock's case—testimony from the observatory's vanished astronomer documenting the purge that preceded the conquest. When an imperial census taker begins asking pointed questions about who touched the clock and when, Felix realizes he is both witness and target. Racing to authenticate and publish the letters before the victors' historians rewrite the record, Felix finds unexpected allies among the observatory's dismissed staff, and in the end chooses to sign his own name to the testimony, trading invisibility for a place in a found family of truth-keepers.
about_author: Kestrel Brightwater is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing seized private papers in post-conflict collections. Their fiction explores what survives official history—and who pays to keep it alive.

chapters.title: The Stopped Hour
chapters.summary: Felix Oyelaran, POV. Summoned under escort to repair the observatory's master clock, Felix keeps his head down, mending gears while imperial officers loiter. Inside the case he finds a hidden bundle of letters sealed with wax. The emotional beat is wary curiosity: his instinct to stay invisible collides with the pull of what he has found.

chapters.title: One Question Too Many
chapters.summary: Felix, POV. A census taker arrives at his workshop asking not just names and trades but where he was on the night the observatory staff disappeared. Felix lies badly, then reads the letters: the astronomer's firsthand account of the purge. Rising dread gives way to resolve—he cannot unknow this.

chapters.title: The Weight of Names
chapters.summary: Felix, POV, with interludes from the census taker's ledger. Felix seeks out the observatory's dismissed housekeeper and a young apprentice left behind, forming a fragile circle of witnesses. The climax comes as imperial historians arrive to seal the archive; Felix must smuggle the letters out during the clock's public restart ceremony, nearly caught as the hour strikes.

chapters.title: On the Record
chapters.summary: Felix, POV. With the city watching the restarted clock, Felix delivers copies of the testimony to foreign correspondents and buries the original beneath the bridge where the astronomer once met her sources. He signs his name to the published account. The resolution is quiet and costly: he loses his anonymity but gains a family bound by shared memory.
